sentences.zh: 曹鼐，字萬鐘，寧晉人。

translations.literal: Cao Nai, styled Wanchong, was a native of Ningjin.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Nai, styled Wanchong, came from Ningjin.

sentences.zh: 少伉爽有大誌，事繼母以孝聞。

translations.literal: From youth he was forthright and high-minded and became known for filial devotion to his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was upright and ambitious, and won renown for the filial way he treated his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，由鄉舉授代州訓導，願授別職，改泰和縣典史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xuande reign he was appointed Instructor at Daizhou through the provincial examination; wishing a different post, he was transferred to be Registrar of Taihe County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuande reign he entered office as Instructor at Daizhou by provincial nomination; preferring another appointment, he was moved to Registrar of Taihe County.

sentences.zh: 七年督工匠至京師，疏乞入試，復中順天鄉試。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, while supervising artisans at the capital, he petitioned to sit the examinations and again passed the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, while overseeing artisans at the capital, he memorialized to take the examinations and again passed the Shuntian provincial test.

sentences.zh: 明年舉進士一甲第一，賜宴禮部。

translations.literal: The next year he took first place in the highest class of the metropolitan examination and was granted a banquet at the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he ranked first in the top tier of the metropolitan examination and was given a feast at the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 進士宴禮部，自鼐始。

translations.literal: The banquet for new metropolitan graduates at the Ministry of Rites began with Nai.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites banquet for new jinshi began with Nai.

sentences.zh: 入翰林，為修撰。

translations.literal: He entered the Hanlin Academy as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin Academy as a Compiler.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong he served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengtong he served as lecturer at the imperial lecture series.

sentences.zh: 《宣宗實錄》成，進侍講，錫三品章服。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of the Xuande Emperor were completed, he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting and given robes of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of the Xuande Emperor were finished, he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting and granted third-rank ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 五年，以楊榮、楊士奇薦，入直文淵閣，參預機務。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on the recommendation of Yang Rong and Yang Shiqi, he entered the Wenyuan Pavilion on permanent duty and participated in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, on the recommendation of Yang Rong and Yang Shiqi, he took up permanent duty in the Wenyuan Pavilion and joined in deliberating on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 鼐為人內剛外和，通達政體。

translations.literal: Nai was stern within and gentle without, and thoroughly versed in governmental principles.
translations.idiomatic: Nai was firm inwardly and mild outwardly, and thoroughly understood how government should work.

sentences.zh: 榮既歿，士奇常病不視事，閣務多決於鼐。

translations.literal: After Rong died, Shiqi was often ill and did not attend to affairs; most decisions of the Grand Secretariat fell to Nai.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong died, Shiqi was often ill and did not handle business, and most Grand Secretariat decisions fell to Nai.

sentences.zh: 帝以為賢，進翰林學士。

translations.literal: The Emperor regarded him as able and promoted him to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor considered him capable and promoted him to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 十年進吏部左侍郎兼學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was advanced to Left Vice Minister of Personnel, retaining his academicianship.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Personnel while retaining his academicianship.

sentences.zh: 十四年七月，也先入寇，中官王振挾帝親征。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year, Esen of the Oirats invaded; the eunuch Wang Zhen induced the Emperor to lead a campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year, Esen of the Oirats invaded; the eunuch Wang Zhen pressed the Emperor to take the field in person.

sentences.zh: 朝臣交章諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Court officials submitted memorial after memorial in remonstrance, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the court submitted memorial after memorial in protest, but he would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 鼐與張益以閣臣扈從。

translations.literal: Nai and Zhang Yi accompanied the expedition as Grand Secretariat ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Nai and Zhang Yi accompanied the campaign as Grand Secretariat ministers.

sentences.zh: 未至大同，士卒已乏糧。

translations.literal: Before they reached Datong, the troops were already short of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Before they reached Datong, the soldiers were already without adequate grain.

sentences.zh: 宋瑛、朱冕全軍沒。

translations.literal: Song Ying and Zhu Mian were wiped out with their entire armies.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ying and Zhu Mian were destroyed with their whole forces.

sentences.zh: 諸臣請班師，振不許，趣諸軍進。

translations.literal: The ministers asked to withdraw the army; Zhen would not permit it and urged the forces forward.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers asked to withdraw the army; Zhen refused and pressed the troops to advance.

sentences.zh: 大將朱勇膝行聽命，尚書鄺埜、王佐跪草中，至暮不得請。

translations.literal: The commander Zhu Yong crawled on his knees to receive orders; the Ministers Kuang Ye and Wang Zuo knelt in the grass, but until evening could not obtain an audience.
translations.idiomatic: The commander Zhu Yong advanced on his knees to receive orders; the Ministers Kuang Ye and Wang Zuo knelt in the grass, yet until evening could not secure a hearing.

sentences.zh: 欽天監正彭德清言天象示警，若前，恐危乘輿。

translations.literal: The Director of the Astronomy Bureau Peng Deqing said the heavens showed warnings: if they went on as before, the imperial carriage might be endangered.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Astronomy Bureau Peng Deqing said the heavens showed warnings: if they proceeded as before, the imperial carriage might be imperiled.

sentences.zh: 振詈曰：「爾何知！

translations.literal: Zhen reviled him, saying: "What do you know!
translations.idiomatic: Zhen cursed him, saying: "What do you know!

sentences.zh: 若有此，亦天命也。

translations.literal: If this should happen, it is also the mandate of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: If that should come to pass, it is likewise Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 」鼐曰：「臣子固不足惜，主上系天下安危，豈可輕進？

translations.literal: Nai said: "We subjects are indeed not worth sparing, but Your Majesty bears the safety of the realm—how can you lightly advance?"
translations.idiomatic: Nai said: "We subjects are not worth sparing, but Your Majesty holds the safety of the realm in your hands—how can you advance so lightly?"

sentences.zh: 」振終不從。

translations.literal: Zhen in the end would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen in the end would not agree.

sentences.zh: 前驅敗報踵至，始懼，欲還。

translations.literal: Reports of defeat from the van arrived one after another; he at last grew afraid and wished to turn back.
translations.idiomatic: Reports of defeat from the advance guard arrived in succession; he at last grew afraid and wished to turn back.

sentences.zh: 定襄侯郭登言於鼐、益曰：「自此趨紫荊，裁四十餘里，駕宜從紫荊入。

translations.literal: Guo Deng, Marquis of Dingxiang, said to Nai and Yi: "From here it is only a little over forty li to Zijing—the carriage ought to enter by Zijing."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Deng, Marquis of Dingxiang, said to Nai and Yi: "From here it is only a little over forty li to Zijing—the imperial carriage ought to enter by Zijing."

sentences.zh: 」振欲邀帝至蔚州幸其第，不聽，復折而東，趨居庸。

translations.literal: Zhen wished to invite the Emperor to Yu Prefecture to visit his own residence; the Emperor did not listen, and they turned east again toward Juyong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen wished to bring the Emperor to Yu Prefecture to visit his own house; the Emperor did not listen, and they turned east again toward Juyong.

sentences.zh: 八月辛酉次土木。

translations.literal: On the xinyou day of the eighth month they halted at Tumu.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day of the eighth month they encamped at Tumu.

sentences.zh: 地高，掘地二丈不及水。

translations.literal: The ground was high; they dug two zhang deep but still did not reach water.
translations.idiomatic: The ground was high; they dug two zhang deep but still did not reach water.

sentences.zh: 瓦剌大至，據南河。

translations.literal: The Oirats came in force and held the south bank of the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Oirats arrived in strength and occupied the south bank of the river.

sentences.zh: 明日佯卻，且遣使通和。

translations.literal: The next day they feigned withdrawal and moreover sent envoys to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they feigned retreat and also sent envoys to discuss peace.

sentences.zh: 帝召鼐草詔答之。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Nai to draft an edict in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Nai to draft an edict in response.

sentences.zh: 振遽令移營就水，行亂。

translations.literal: Zhen abruptly ordered the camp moved toward the water, and the march fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen abruptly ordered the camp shifted toward the water, and the army fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 寇騎蹂陣入，帝突圍不得出，擁以去。

translations.literal: Enemy horsemen trampled through the formation; the Emperor could not break out and was seized and carried away.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy horsemen overran the formation; the Emperor could not break out and was seized and borne away.

sentences.zh: 鼐、益等俱及於難。

translations.literal: Nai, Yi, and the others all met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Nai, Yi, and the others all perished in the disaster.

sentences.zh: 景帝立，贈鼐少傅、吏部尚書、文淵閣大學士，謚文襄，官其子恩大理評事。

translations.literal: When the Jing Emperor ascended the throne, Nai was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, with the posthumous title Wenxiang; his son En was given office as Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing Emperor took the throne, Nai was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, with the posthumous title Wenxiang; his son En was appointed Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，加贈太傅，改謚文忠，復官其孫榮錦衣百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ying restored the throne, he was further posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and his posthumous title changed to Wenzhong; his grandson Rong was again given office as commander of one hundred households in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ying regained the throne, Nai was further posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and his posthumous title changed to Wenzhong; his grandson Rong was again appointed a commander of one hundred households in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 鼐弟鼎進士，歷吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: Nai's younger brother Ding was a metropolitan graduate and served successively as Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Nai's younger brother Ding was a metropolitan graduate and rose to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.

sentences.zh: 張益，字士謙，江寧人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, styled Shiqian, was a native of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, styled Shiqian, came from Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 永樂十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongle he became a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yongle he passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士授中書舍人，改大理評事。

translations.literal: From Student of the Hanlin he was appointed Secretariat Drafter, then transferred to be Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin Bachelor he was appointed Secretariat Drafter, then moved to Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 與修《宣宗實錄》成，改修撰。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of the Xuande Emperor were completed, he was made Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of the Xuande Emperor were finished, he was made Compiler.

sentences.zh: 博學強記，詩文操筆立就，三楊雅重之。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned and had a strong memory; his poetry and prose were completed as soon as he took up the brush, and the Three Yangs held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned and had a powerful memory; his verse and prose were finished the moment he set brush to paper, and the Three Yangs greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 尋進侍讀學士，正統十四年入文淵閣。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting and in the fourteenth year of Zhengtong entered the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Reader-in-Waiting and in the fourteenth year of Zhengtong entered the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 未三月，遽蒙難以歿。

translations.literal: In less than three months he suddenly met disaster and died.
translations.idiomatic: In less than three months he suddenly met disaster and died.

sentences.zh: 景帝立，贈學士，謚文僖。

translations.literal: When the Jing Emperor ascended the throne, he was posthumously given the title of Academician, with the posthumous name Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing Emperor took the throne, he was posthumously granted the title of Academician, with the posthumous name Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 曾孫琮進士。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Cong was a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Cong passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初歷官南京右都御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he served successively as Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he rose to Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 鄺埜，字孟質，宜章人。

translations.literal: Kuang Ye, styled Mengzhi, was a native of Yizhang.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang Ye, styled Mengzhi, came from Yizhang.

sentences.zh: 永樂九年進士，授監察御史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongle he became a metropolitan graduate and was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yongle he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 成祖在北京，或奏南京鈔法為豪民沮壞，帝遣埜廉視。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu Emperor was at Beijing, someone reported that the paper-money system at Nanjing was being obstructed and ruined by powerful families; the Emperor sent Ye to investigate on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: While the Chengzu Emperor was at Beijing, someone reported that Nanjing's paper-money system was being blocked and ruined by powerful families; the Emperor sent Ye to inspect on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 眾謂將起大獄，埜執一二市豪歸。

translations.literal: Many said a major prosecution would follow; Ye seized only one or two market magnates and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Many expected a major prosecution; Ye took only one or two market magnates and returned.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「市人聞令震懼，鈔法通矣。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "When the market people heard the order they were shaken with fear, and the paper-money system is now unimpeded."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "When the market people heard the order they trembled with fear, and the paper-money system is flowing again."

sentences.zh: 」事遂已。

translations.literal: The matter was thereupon closed.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was thereupon closed.

sentences.zh: 倭犯遼東，戍守失律者百余人，皆應死。

translations.literal: When the Wo pirates raided Liaodong, more than a hundred men who had failed in garrison duty were all liable to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Japanese raiders struck Liaodong, more than a hundred men who had failed in garrison duty were all subject to the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 命埜按問，具言可矜狀，帝為宥之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Ye to investigate; he set forth fully the grounds for mercy, and the Emperor pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Ye to review the cases; he fully stated grounds for compassion, and the Emperor spared them.

sentences.zh: 營造北京，執役者鉅萬，命埜稽省，病者多不死。

translations.literal: In constructing Beijing, those pressed into labor numbered in the tens of thousands; the Emperor ordered Ye to audit the rolls, and many who were ill did not die.
translations.idiomatic: In building Beijing, those conscripted for labor ran to tens of thousands; the Emperor ordered Ye to audit the rolls, and many who were ill were not left to die.

sentences.zh: 十六年有言秦民群聚謀不軌者，擢埜陜西按察副使，敕以便宜調兵剿捕。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year someone reported that the people of Qin had gathered in groups plotting sedition; Ye was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Shaanxi Surveillance Commission and ordered, as circumstances required, to mobilize troops to suppress and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year someone reported that Qin people had gathered plotting sedition; Ye was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Shaanxi Surveillance Commission and charged, as circumstances required, to mobilize troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 埜白其誣，詔誅妄言者。

translations.literal: Ye showed the charge was false, and an edict ordered the execution of the false accuser.
translations.idiomatic: Ye proved the accusation false, and an edict ordered the false accuser put to death.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年振關中饑。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuande he relieved famine in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xuande he relieved famine in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 在陜久，刑政清簡。

translations.literal: Having long been in Shaanxi, his punishments and administration were clear and simple.
translations.idiomatic: After long service in Shaanxi, his criminal justice and administration were clear and restrained.

sentences.zh: 父憂服除，擢應天府尹。

translations.literal: When mourning for his father ended, he was promoted to Prefect of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning for his father ended, he was promoted to Prefect of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 蠲苛急政，市征田稅皆酌其平。

translations.literal: He abolished harsh and urgent measures; market levies and field taxes were all set at moderate rates.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished harsh urgent measures; market levies and field taxes were all adjusted to fair levels.

sentences.zh: 正統元年進兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengtong he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明年，尚書王驥出督軍，埜獨任部事。

translations.literal: The next year, when Minister Wang Ji went out to supervise the army, Ye alone bore the affairs of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Minister Wang Ji went out to supervise the armies, Ye alone handled the ministry's business.

sentences.zh: 時邊陲多警，將帥乏人，埜請令中外博舉謀略材武士，以備任使。

translations.literal: At the time the frontier was often alarmed and commanders were lacking; Ye asked that inside and outside the court men of strategy and martial talent be broadly recommended to fill appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier was then often under alert and generals were scarce; Ye asked that men of strategy and martial talent be broadly recommended throughout the court and country for appointment.

sentences.zh: 六年，山東災。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Shandong suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Shandong suffered disaster.

sentences.zh: 埜請寬民間孳牧馬賠償之令，以蘇其力。

translations.literal: Ye asked that the order requiring commoners to compensate for lost stud horses be relaxed, to restore their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Ye asked that the rule requiring commoners to compensate for lost stud horses be eased, to restore their strength.

sentences.zh: 十年進尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to Minister.

sentences.zh: 舊例諸衛自百戶以下當代者，必就試京師，道遠無資者，終身不得代。

translations.literal: By old regulation, those in the guards from company commanders down who were due for succession had to be examined at the capital; those who lived far and lacked funds might never obtain succession in their lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation, guard officers from company commanders down who were due for succession had to be examined at the capital; those far away without means might never obtain succession in their lifetime.

sentences.zh: 埜請就令各都司試之，人以為便。

translations.literal: Ye asked that they be examined at their respective regional commands; people regarded this as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Ye asked that they be examined at their respective regional commands; people regarded this as convenient.

sentences.zh: 瓦剌也先勢盛，埜請為備，又與廷臣議上方略，請增大同兵，擇智謀大臣巡視西北邊務。

translations.literal: Esen of the Oirats grew powerful; Ye asked that preparations be made, and with court ministers discussed strategy, requesting increased troops at Datong and that a wise and able minister be chosen to tour northwest frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As Esen of the Oirats grew powerful, Ye asked for preparations and, with court ministers, discussed strategy, requesting more troops at Datong and that a wise minister be chosen to inspect northwest frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋又請罷京營兵修城之役，令休息以備緩急。

translations.literal: He soon also asked to halt the capital-garrison soldiers' wall-repair labor and let them rest to meet emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: He soon also asked to stop the capital garrison's wall-repair labor and let them rest against emergencies.

sentences.zh: 時不能用。

translations.literal: At the time this could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this could not be adopted.

sentences.zh: 也先入寇，王振主親征，不與外廷議可否。

translations.literal: When Esen invaded, Wang Zhen insisted on a personal campaign and did not consult the outer court on whether it was advisable.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen invaded, Wang Zhen insisted on a personal campaign and did not consult the outer court on whether it should proceed.

sentences.zh: 詔下，埜上疏言：「也先入犯，一邊將足制之。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Ye submitted a memorial saying: "Esen has come in to raid; a single frontier general is enough to check him.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Ye memorialized: "Esen has come raiding; one frontier general is enough to contain him.

sentences.zh: 陛下為宗廟社稷主，奈何不自重。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is lord of the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain—how can you fail to value yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is lord of the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain—how can you fail to cherish yourself?"

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 既扈駕出關，力請回鑾。

translations.literal: Once he had accompanied the imperial procession beyond the passes, he pressed strongly for the carriage to return.
translations.idiomatic: After accompanying the imperial procession beyond the passes, he pressed strongly for the carriage to return.

sentences.zh: 振怒，令與戶部尚書王佐皆隨大營。

translations.literal: Zhen was angry and ordered him and Minister of Revenue Wang Zuo both to follow the main camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was angry and ordered him and Minister of Revenue Wang Zuo both to follow the main camp.

sentences.zh: 埜墮馬幾殆，或勸留懷來城就醫。

translations.literal: Ye fell from his horse and nearly died; some urged him to remain at Huailai City to seek medical care.
translations.idiomatic: Ye fell from his horse and nearly died; some urged him to stay at Huailai City for treatment.

sentences.zh: 埜曰：「至尊在行，敢托疾自便乎？

translations.literal: Ye said: "The supreme sovereign is on the march—how dare I plead illness for my own convenience?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye said: "The supreme sovereign is on the march—how dare I plead illness for my own convenience?"

sentences.zh: 」車駕次宣府，朱勇敗沒。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession reached Xuanfu, Zhu Yong was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession reached Xuanfu, Zhu Yong was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 埜請疾驅入關，嚴兵為殿。

translations.literal: Ye asked that they hurry through the passes and array troops as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: Ye asked that they hurry through the passes and array troops as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was received.
translations.idiomatic: No reply was received.

sentences.zh: 又詣行在申請。

translations.literal: He again went to the traveling palace to petition.
translations.idiomatic: He again went to the traveling palace to petition.

sentences.zh: 振怒曰：「腐儒安知兵事，再言者死！

translations.literal: Zhen said angrily: "What do decayed scholars know of military affairs—speak again and you die!
translations.idiomatic: Zhen raged: "What do pedantic scholars know of war—say it again and you die!

sentences.zh: 」埜曰：「我為社稷生靈言，何懼？

translations.literal: Ye said: "I speak for the altars of state and the people—what is there to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye said: "I speak for the realm and the people—what have I to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」振叱左右扶出。

translations.literal: Zhen shouted for attendants to support him out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen ordered attendants to haul him out.

sentences.zh: 埜與佐對泣帳中。

translations.literal: Ye and Zuo wept facing each other in the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Ye and Zuo wept together in the tent.

sentences.zh: 明日，師覆，埜死，年六十五。

translations.literal: The next day the army was destroyed; Ye died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the army was destroyed; Ye died at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 埜為人勤廉端謹，性至孝。

translations.literal: Ye was diligent, incorrupt, upright, and cautious in conduct, and by nature deeply filial.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was diligent, incorrupt, upright, and cautious, and by nature profoundly filial.

sentences.zh: 父子輔為句容教官，教埜甚嚴。

translations.literal: His father Fu was Instructor at Jurong and taught Ye very strictly.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu was Instructor at Jurong and taught Ye with great strictness.

sentences.zh: 埜在陜久，思一見父，乃謀聘父為鄉試考官。

translations.literal: Ye had long been in Shaanxi and wished to see his father once; he therefore planned to hire his father as examiner for the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Long in Shaanxi, Ye longed to see his father and planned to engage him as examiner for the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 父怒曰：「子居憲司，而父為考官，何以防閑？

translations.literal: His father said angrily: "You hold office in the Surveillance Commission while your father is examiner—how can propriety be guarded?"
translations.idiomatic: His father stormed: "You sit in the Surveillance Commission while your father is examiner—how is that to be kept proper?"

sentences.zh: 」馳書責之。

translations.literal: He sent a letter at speed to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a swift letter rebuking him.

sentences.zh: 埜又嘗寄父褐，復貽書責曰：「汝掌刑名，當洗冤釋滯，以無忝任使，何從得此褐，乃以汙我。

translations.literal: Ye once also sent his father a brown garment and again wrote to rebuke him, saying: "You hold criminal justice— you should clear wrongs and release the detained, so as not to fail your charge; how did you obtain this garment to stain me?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye once sent his father a brown robe and wrote again to rebuke him: "You hold criminal justice—you should clear wrongs and release the detained, not fail your charge; how did you get this robe to stain me?"

sentences.zh: 」封還之。

translations.literal: He sealed it and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed it and sent it back.

sentences.zh: 埜奉書跪誦，泣受教。

translations.literal: Ye received the letter, knelt and recited it, and weeping accepted the instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Ye received the letter, knelt to read it aloud, and weeping took the lesson.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，贈埜少保，官其子儀為主事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign Ye was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian; his son Yi was given office as Director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingtai, Ye was posthumously made Junior Guardian; his son Yi was appointed Director.

sentences.zh: 成化初，謚忠肅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he was given the posthumous title Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chenghua he received the posthumous title Zhongsu.

sentences.zh: 王佐，海豐人。

translations.literal: Wang Zuo was a native of Haifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zuo came from Haifeng.

sentences.zh: 永樂中舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the Yongle reign he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 卒業太學，以學行聞，擢吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He graduated from the Imperial Academy, became known for learning and conduct, and was promoted to Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He graduated from the Imperial Academy, won renown for learning and conduct, and was raised to Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.

sentences.zh: 器宇凝重，奏對詳雅，為宣宗所簡註。

translations.literal: His bearing was grave; his memorials and responses were detailed and elegant, and the Xuande Emperor singled him out for notice.
translations.idiomatic: He was grave in bearing; his memorials and responses were thorough and refined, and the Xuande Emperor marked him out.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年，超拜戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande he was abruptly promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuande he was abruptly promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以太倉、臨清、德州、淮、徐諸倉多積弊，敕佐巡視。

translations.literal: Because the granaries at Taicang, Linqing, Dezhou, Huai, and Xu had many accumulated abuses, the Emperor ordered Zuo to inspect them.
translations.idiomatic: Because granaries at Taicang, Linqing, Dezhou, Huai, and Xu harbored many abuses, the Emperor ordered Zuo to inspect them.

sentences.zh: 平江伯陳瑄言，漕卒十二萬人，歲漕艱苦，乞僉南方民如軍數，更番轉運。

translations.literal: The Earl of Pingjiang Chen Xuan said that the 120,000 transport laborers found annual grain transport bitterly hard and asked to conscript southern commoners in numbers like the army, rotating in turns for transport.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xuan, Earl of Pingjiang, said 120,000 transport laborers found annual grain transport crushing and asked to conscript southern commoners in army-like numbers, rotating for transport.

sentences.zh: 詔佐就瑄及黃福議之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zuo to go to Chen Xuan and Huang Fu to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zuo to consult Chen Xuan and Huang Fu.

sentences.zh: 佐還奏，東南民力已困，議遂寢。

translations.literal: Zuo returned and memorialized that the strength of the southeast was already exhausted; the proposal was thereupon shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo returned and reported southeastern strength already spent; the plan was shelved.

sentences.zh: 受命治通州至直沽河道。

translations.literal: He was charged to manage the waterways from Tongzhou to Zhigu.
translations.idiomatic: He was charged to manage the waterways from Tongzhou to Zhigu.

sentences.zh: 已，赴宣府議屯田事宜。

translations.literal: Later he went to Xuanfu to discuss garrison-farming affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went to Xuanfu to discuss garrison-farming affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，尚書劉中敷得罪，召理部事，尋進尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Minister Liu Zhongfu offended and was punished; Zuo was summoned to handle ministry affairs and soon promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Minister Liu Zhongfu offended and was punished; Zuo was summoned to run the ministry and soon made Minister.

sentences.zh: 十一年承詔訊安鄉伯張安兄弟爭祿事，坐與法司相諉，被劾下吏，獲釋。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he received an edict to investigate the dispute over stipends between the brothers Zhang An, Earl of Anxiang; for shifting blame with the judicial offices he was impeached and sent to the magistrates, then released.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was ordered to investigate the stipend dispute of Zhang An, Earl of Anxiang, and his brother; for shifting blame with the judicial offices he was impeached, sent to the magistrates, then released.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅四出，耗費動以鉅萬，府庫空虛。

translations.literal: At the time armies marched in all directions and expenditures often ran to tens of millions; the treasury was empty.
translations.idiomatic: Armies then marched everywhere and costs often ran to tens of millions; the treasury was empty.

sentences.zh: 佐從容調劑，節縮有方。

translations.literal: Zuo calmly adjusted matters and economized with method.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo calmly adjusted affairs and economized with skill.

sentences.zh: 在戶部久，不為赫赫名，而寬厚有度，政務糾紛，未嘗廢學，人稱其君子。

translations.literal: Long in the Ministry of Revenue, he did not seek a loud reputation, yet was generous and measured; though official business was tangled, he never abandoned study, and people called him a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Long in Revenue, he sought no loud fame yet was generous and measured; though business piled up, he never quit study, and men called him a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 土木之變，與鄺埜、丁鉉、王永和、鄧棨同死難。

translations.literal: At the Tumu disaster he died with Kuang Ye, Ding Xian, Wang Yonghe, and Deng Qi.
translations.idiomatic: At Tumu he died with Kuang Ye, Ding Xian, Wang Yonghe, and Deng Qi.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，官其子道戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian; his son Dao was given office as Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Junior Guardian; his son Dao was appointed Director in Revenue.

sentences.zh: 成化初，謚忠簡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he was given the posthumous title Zhongjian.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chenghua he received the posthumous title Zhongjian.

sentences.zh: 丁鉉，字用濟，豐城人。

translations.literal: Ding Xian, styled Yongji, was a native of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Xian, styled Yongji, came from Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 永樂中進士。

translations.literal: In the Yongle reign he became a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle he passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 授太常博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 歷工、刑、吏三部員外郎，進刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Director in the Ministries of Works, Punishments, and Personnel, and was advanced to Director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Vice Director posts in Works, Punishments, and Personnel, then became Director of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 正統三年超拜刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong he was abruptly promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengtong he was abruptly promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 九年出理四川茶課，奏減其常數，以俟豐歲。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he went out to administer Sichuan tea duties and memorialized to reduce the regular quota, to wait for abundant years.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he went to administer Sichuan tea duties and memorialized to cut the regular quota until abundant years.

sentences.zh: 振饑江淮及山東、河南，民鹹賴之。

translations.literal: He relieved famine in Jianghuai and in Shandong and Henan; the people all relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved famine in Jianghuai, Shandong, and Henan; the people all relied on him.

sentences.zh: 平居恂恂若無能，臨事悉治辦。

translations.literal: In ordinary times he was respectful and seemed incapable; when affairs came he handled them all.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary times he seemed mild and incapable; when business came he handled everything.

sentences.zh: 從征歿，贈刑部尚書，官其子琥大理評事。

translations.literal: He died on the campaign and was posthumously made Minister of Punishments; his son Hu was given office as Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the campaign and was posthumously made Minister of Punishments; his son Hu was appointed Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 後謚襄湣。

translations.literal: Later he was given the posthumous title Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: Later he received the posthumous title Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 王永和，字以正，昆山人。

translations.literal: Wang Yonghe, styled Yizheng, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yonghe, styled Yizheng, came from Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 少至孝。

translations.literal: From youth he was profoundly filial.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was profoundly filial.

sentences.zh: 父病伏枕十八年，侍湯藥無少懈。

translations.literal: His father lay ill in bed eighteen years; he attended medicines without the least slackening.
translations.idiomatic: His father lay ill eighteen years; he tended medicines without slackening.

sentences.zh: 永樂中舉於鄉，歷嚴州、饒州訓導。

translations.literal: In the Yongle reign he passed the provincial examination and served successively as Instructor at Yanzhou and Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle he passed the provincial examination and served as Instructor at Yanzhou and Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 以蹇義薦，為兵科給事中。

translations.literal: On Jian Yi's recommendation he became Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for War.
translations.idiomatic: On Jian Yi's recommendation he became Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for War.

sentences.zh: 嘗劾都督王彧鎮薊州縱寇，及錦衣馬順不法事。

translations.literal: He once impeached Commander Wang Yu for garrisoning Jizhou and letting raiders run free, and the Embroidered-Uniform Guard Ma Shun for unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He once impeached Commander Wang Yu for garrisoning Jizhou and letting raiders roam, and Ma Shun of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard for unlawful acts.

sentences.zh: 持節冊韓世子妃，糾中官蹇傲罪。

translations.literal: Bearing credentials he invested the consort of the Heir of Han and impeached the eunuch Jian Ao.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing credentials he invested the Han heir's consort and impeached the eunuch Jian Ao.

sentences.zh: 以勁直聞。

translations.literal: He became known for firm uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: He became known for firm uprightness.

sentences.zh: 正統六年進都給事中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong he was promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhengtong he was promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 八年擢工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was raised to Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was raised to Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 從征歿，贈工部尚書，官其子汝賢大理評事。

translations.literal: He died on the campaign and was posthumously made Minister of Works; his son Ruxian was given office as Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the campaign and was posthumously made Minister of Works; his son Ruxian was appointed Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 後謚襄敏。

translations.literal: Later he was given the posthumous title Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: Later he received the posthumous title Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 鄧棨，字孟擴，南城人。

translations.literal: Deng Qi, styled Mengkuo, was a native of Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qi, styled Mengkuo, came from Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 永樂末年進士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongle reign he became a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongle he passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 授監察御史，奉敕巡按蘇、松諸府。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor and, by imperial order, toured and inspected the prefectures of Suzhou and Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Investigating Censor and by imperial order inspected Suzhou and Songjiang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 期滿將代去，父老赴闕乞留，得請。

translations.literal: When his term ended and a successor was to replace him, elders of the people went to court begging he be kept; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, local elders went to court begging he stay; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 旋以憂去。

translations.literal: Soon after he left on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he left on mourning.

sentences.zh: 宣德十年，陜西闕按察使，詔廷臣舉清慎有威望者。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xuande the post of Surveillance Commissioner in Shaanxi was vacant; an edict ordered court ministers to recommend men who were pure, cautious, and of standing.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xuande Shaanxi lacked a Surveillance Commissioner; an edict ordered ministers to recommend men pure, cautious, and of standing.

sentences.zh: 楊士奇薦棨，遂以命之。

translations.literal: Yang Shiqi recommended Qi, and he was thereupon appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shiqi recommended Qi, and he was appointed.

sentences.zh: 正統十年入為右副都御史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhengtong he entered office as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhengtong he entered as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 北征扈從，師出居庸關，疏請回鑾，以兵事專屬大將。

translations.literal: On the northern campaign he accompanied the guard; when the army passed Juyong Pass he memorialized asking the carriage to return and that military affairs be entrusted solely to the commander.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern campaign he accompanied the guard; when the army passed Juyong he memorialized for the carriage to return and military affairs to rest with the commander alone.

sentences.zh: 至宣府、大同，復再上章。

translations.literal: At Xuanfu and Datong he again submitted memorials.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanfu and Datong he submitted memorials again.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: No reply was received on any.
translations.idiomatic: None received reply.

sentences.zh: 及遇變，同行者語曰：「吾輩可自脫去。

translations.literal: When disaster struck, a companion said: "We can slip away ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck, a companion said: "We can save ourselves.

sentences.zh: 」棨曰：「鑾輿失所，我尚何歸！

translations.literal: Qi said: "The imperial carriage is lost—where shall I return!
translations.idiomatic: Qi said: "The imperial carriage is lost—where can I go!

sentences.zh: 主辱臣死，分也。

translations.literal: When the lord is shamed the minister dies—that is his portion.
translations.idiomatic: When the lord is shamed the minister dies—that is duty.

sentences.zh: 」遂死。

translations.literal: He thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon died.

sentences.zh: 贈右都御史，官其子常大理評事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Right Censor-in-Chief; his son Chang was given office as Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Right Censor-in-Chief; his son Chang was appointed Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 後謚襄敏。

translations.literal: Later he was given the posthumous title Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: Later he received the posthumous title Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 英宗之出也，備文武百官以行。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ying went out, civil and military officials of every rank accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ying marched out, civil and military officials of every rank went with him.

sentences.zh: 六師覆於土木，將相大臣及從官死者不可勝數。

translations.literal: The six armies were destroyed at Tumu; generals, ministers, and attendant officials who died could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: The six armies were destroyed at Tumu; generals, ministers, and attendants who died were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 英國公張輔及諸侯伯自有傳。

translations.literal: The Duke of Ying Zhang Fu and the marquises and earls have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu, Duke of Ying, and the marquises and earls have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 其余姓氏可考者，卿寺則龔全安、黃養正、戴慶祖、王一居、劉容、淩壽；

translations.literal: Of the rest whose surnames can be verified, among ministers and directors were Gong Quan'an, Huang Yangzheng, Dai Qingzu, Wang Yiju, Liu Rong, and Ling Shou;
translations.idiomatic: Of others whose names are known, among ministers and directors were Gong Quan'an, Huang Yangzheng, Dai Qingzu, Wang Yiju, Liu Rong, and Ling Shou;

sentences.zh: 給事、御史則包良佐、姚銑、鮑輝、張洪、黃裳、魏貞、夏誠、申祐、尹竑、童存德、孫慶、林祥鳳；

translations.literal: among supervising secretaries and censors were Bao Liangzuo, Yao Xian, Bao Hui, Zhang Hong, Huang Shang, Wei Zhen, Xia Cheng, Shen You, Yin Hong, Tong Cunde, Sun Qing, and Lin Xiangfeng;
translations.idiomatic: among supervising secretaries and censors were Bao Liangzuo, Yao Xian, Bao Hui, Zhang Hong, Huang Shang, Wei Zhen, Xia Cheng, Shen You, Yin Hong, Tong Cunde, Sun Qing, and Lin Xiangfeng;

sentences.zh: 庶寮則齊汪、馮學明、王健、程思溫、程式、逯端、俞鑒、張瑭、鄭瑄、俞拱、潘澄、錢昺、馬預、尹昌、羅如墉、劉信、李恭、石玉。

translations.literal: among lower officials were Qi Wang, Feng Xueming, Wang Jian, Cheng Siwen, Cheng Shi, Lu Duan, Yu Jian, Zhang Tang, Zheng Xuan, Yu Gong, Pan Cheng, Qian Bing, Ma Yu, Yin Chang, Luo Ruyong, Liu Xin, Li Gong, and Shi Yu.
translations.idiomatic: among lower officials were Qi Wang, Feng Xueming, Wang Jian, Cheng Siwen, Cheng Shi, Lu Duan, Yu Jian, Zhang Tang, Zheng Xuan, Yu Gong, Pan Cheng, Qian Bing, Ma Yu, Yin Chang, Luo Ruyong, Liu Xin, Li Gong, and Shi Yu.

sentences.zh: 景帝立，既贈恤諸大臣，自給事、御史以下，皆降敕褒美，錄其子為國子生，一時恤典綦備雲。

translations.literal: When the Jing Emperor ascended the throne, after posthumous favors for the great ministers, from supervising secretaries and censors down edicts of praise were all issued, their sons enrolled as students of the Imperial Academy, and for a time condolence rites were complete indeed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing Emperor took the throne, after enfeoffing the great ministers, from supervising secretaries and censors down edicts praised them and enrolled their sons in the Imperial Academy—condolence rites were then complete indeed.

sentences.zh: 龔全安，蘭溪人。

translations.literal: Gong Quan'an was a native of Lanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Quan'an came from Lanxi.

sentences.zh: 進士，授工科給事中，累遷左通政。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate, he was appointed Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Works and was promoted successively to Left Vice Commissioner of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: A metropolitan graduate, he was appointed Supervising Secretary for Works and rose to Left Vice Commissioner of Transmission.

translations.idiomatic: Ning urged Esen to raid Ningxia westward, seize horses, and drive to the south Yangzi, settling the Emperor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 彬、銘謂帝曰：「天寒道遠，陛下又不能騎，空取凍饑。

translations.literal: Bin and Ming said to the Emperor: "The weather is cold and the road long; Your Majesty cannot ride—you would only take cold and hunger for nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Bin and Ming told the Emperor: "Cold weather and a long road—you cannot ride; you would only freeze and starve for nothing."

sentences.zh: 且至彼而諸將不納，奈何？

translations.literal: And if you arrive and the generals will not receive you, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: And if you arrive and generals will not receive you, what then?"

sentences.zh: 」帝止寧計。

translations.literal: The Emperor stopped Ning's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor stopped Ning's plan.

sentences.zh: 寧又欲殺二人，皆帝力解而止。

translations.literal: Ning again wished to kill the two; both times the Emperor forcefully intervened and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Ning again wished to kill them; both times the Emperor forcefully stopped it.

sentences.zh: 也先將獻妹於帝，彬請駕旋而後聘，帝竟辭之。

translations.literal: When Esen was about to offer his sister to the Emperor, Bin asked that the carriage return before betrothal; the Emperor in the end declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen would offer his sister, Bin asked the carriage return before betrothal; the Emperor declined.

sentences.zh: 也先惡彬、銘二人，欲殺者屢矣。

translations.literal: Esen hated Bin and Ming and several times wished to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Esen hated Bin and Ming and several times wished to kill them.

sentences.zh: 一日縛彬至曠埜，將支解之。

translations.literal: One day he bound Bin and brought him to open country to dismember him.
translations.idiomatic: One day he bound Bin in open country to dismember him.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，如失左右手，急趨救，乃免。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, it was as if he had lost his hands; he hurried to save him and Bin was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heard and rushed as if he had lost his hands; Bin was spared.

sentences.zh: 彬嘗中寒，帝憂甚，以身壓其背，汗浹而愈。

translations.literal: Bin once suffered cold affliction; the Emperor was deeply worried and pressed his body on Bin's back until sweat soaked through and he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Bin once suffered severe cold; the Emperor pressed his body on Bin's back until sweat soaked through and he recovered.

sentences.zh: 帝居漠北期年，視彬猶骨肉也。

translations.literal: The Emperor dwelt north of the desert a full year and regarded Bin as bone and flesh.
translations.idiomatic: A full year north of the desert, the Emperor regarded Bin as kin.

sentences.zh: 及帝還京，景帝僅授彬錦衣試百戶。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned to the capital, the Jing Emperor gave Bin only trial command of one hundred households in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor returned, the Jing Emperor gave Bin only trial command of one hundred households in the Guard.

sentences.zh: 天順復辟，擢指揮僉事。

translations.literal: When Tianshun restored the throne he was raised to Assistant Commander.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianshun's restoration he was raised to Assistant Commander.

sentences.zh: 尋進同知。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was advanced to Vice Commander.

sentences.zh: 帝眷彬甚，奏請無不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor favored Bin greatly; whatever he memorialized was never refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor favored Bin greatly; whatever he asked was granted.

sentences.zh: 內閣商輅既罷，彬乞得其居第。

translations.literal: After Shang Lu of the Grand Secretariat was dismissed, Bin asked for his residence.
translations.idiomatic: After Grand Secretariat minister Shang Lu was dismissed, Bin asked for his residence.

sentences.zh: 既又以湫隘，乞官為別建，帝亦報從。

translations.literal: Finding it cramped, he asked that officials build another residence separately; the Emperor also approved.
translations.idiomatic: Finding it cramped, he asked officials to build him another house; the Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 彬娶妻，命外戚孫顯宗主之，賜予優渥。

translations.literal: When Bin took a wife, the Emperor ordered the maternal relative Sun Xianzong to preside and gave lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin married, the Emperor had maternal relative Sun Xianzong preside and gave lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 時召入曲宴，敘患難時事，歡洽如故時。

translations.literal: He was often summoned to private feasts to recount affairs of hardship; joy flowed as in old times.
translations.idiomatic: He was often summoned to private feasts to recount their hardships; joy flowed as in old times.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月進指揮使，與都指揮僉事王喜同掌衛事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year he was advanced to Commander and, with Assistant Regional Commander Wang Xi, jointly managed guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That twelfth month he was advanced to Commander and, with Assistant Regional Commander Wang Xi, jointly ran the Guard.

sentences.zh: 二人嘗受中官夏時囑，私遣百戶季福偵事江西。

translations.literal: The two had once accepted instructions from the eunuch Xia Shi and privately sent Commander Ji Fu to spy on affairs in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The two had accepted instructions from eunuch Xia Shi and privately sent Commander Ji Fu to spy in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 福者，帝乳媼夫也。

translations.literal: Fu was the husband of the Emperor's wet nurse.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was the husband of the Emperor's wet nurse.

sentences.zh: 詔問誰所遣，二人請罪。

translations.literal: An edict asked who had sent him; the two pleaded guilty.
translations.idiomatic: An edict asked who had sent him; the two pleaded guilty.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此必有主使者。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "There must be a master behind this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Someone must be behind this.

sentences.zh: 」遂下福吏，得二人受囑狀。

translations.literal: Ji Fu was sent to the magistrates, and proof was obtained that the two had accepted instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Fu was sent to the magistrates, and proof the two had accepted instructions was obtained.

sentences.zh: 所司請治時及二人罪。

translations.literal: The responsible offices asked to punish Shi and the two.
translations.idiomatic: The offices asked to punish Shi and the two.

sentences.zh: 帝宥時，二人贖徒還職，而詔自今受囑遣官者，必殺無赦。

translations.literal: The Emperor pardoned Shi; the two redeemed punishment as convict laborers and returned to office, while an edict declared that from now on any official who accepted instructions to dispatch men must be executed without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pardoned Shi; the two redeemed labor and returned to office, while an edict declared that hereafter any official accepting instructions to dispatch men must be executed without pardon.

sentences.zh: 已而坐失囚，喜解職，彬遂掌衛事。

translations.literal: Later, for sitting by while a prisoner escaped, Xi was removed from office and Bin thereupon managed guard affairs alone.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for letting a prisoner escape, Xi was removed and Bin alone managed guard affairs.

sentences.zh: 五年秋，以平曹欽功，進都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year, for merit in pacifying Cao Qin's rebellion, he was advanced to Assistant Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year's autumn, for pacifying Cao Qin's rebellion, he was advanced to Assistant Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 時門達恃帝寵，勢傾朝野。

translations.literal: At the time Men Da relied on the Emperor's favor and his power tilted the court.
translations.idiomatic: Men Da then relied on imperial favor and his power tilted the court.

sentences.zh: 廷臣多下之，彬獨不為屈。

translations.literal: Many court ministers bowed to him; Bin alone would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Many ministers bowed to him; Bin alone would not yield.

sentences.zh: 達誣以罪，請逮治。

translations.literal: Da framed charges against him and asked that he be arrested and tried.
translations.idiomatic: Da framed charges and asked he be arrested and tried.

sentences.zh: 帝欲法行，語之曰：「任汝往治，但以活袁彬還我。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished the law to run its course and told him: "I leave you to try the case, but bring Yuan Bin back alive to me."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished the law enforced and told him: "Try the case, but bring Yuan Bin back alive."

sentences.zh: 」達遂鍛煉成獄。

translations.literal: Da thereupon forged evidence into a completed case.
translations.idiomatic: Da forged evidence into a completed case.

sentences.zh: 賴漆工楊塤訟冤，獄得解。

translations.literal: Thanks to the lacquerer Yang Kan pleading injustice, the case was dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to lacquerer Yang Kan pleading injustice, the case was dissolved.

sentences.zh: 然猶調南京錦衣衛，帶俸閑住。

translations.literal: Yet Bin was still transferred to the Nanjing Embroidered-Uniform Guard, drawing salary while idle.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Bin was transferred to the Nanjing Guard, drawing salary while idle.

sentences.zh: 語詳《達傳》。

translations.literal: The account is detailed in the biography of Da.
translations.idiomatic: Details appear in the biography of Men Da.

sentences.zh: 越二月，英宗崩，達得罪，貶官都勻。

translations.literal: Two months later Emperor Ying died; Da offended and was demoted to an office at Duyun.
translations.idiomatic: Two months later Emperor Ying died; Da offended and was demoted to Duyun.

sentences.zh: 召彬復原職，仍掌衛事。

translations.literal: Bin was summoned back to his original post and again managed guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was summoned back to his original post and again ran the Guard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，達征下獄，充軍南丹。

translations.literal: Before long Da was arrested on campaign and banished to military service at Nandan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Da was arrested on campaign and banished to Nandan.

sentences.zh: 彬餞之於郊，饋以贐。

translations.literal: Bin saw him off in the suburbs and gave parting gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Bin saw him off beyond the walls and gave parting gifts.

sentences.zh: 成化初，進都指揮同知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he was advanced to Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: At Chenghua's beginning he was advanced to Vice Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 久之，進都指揮使。

translations.literal: After long service he was advanced to Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he was advanced to Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 先是，掌錦衣衛者，率張權勢，罔財賄。

translations.literal: Earlier, those who managed the Embroidered-Uniform Guard generally flaunted power and sought bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Guard commanders generally flaunted power and sought bribes.

sentences.zh: 彬任職久，行事安靜。

translations.literal: Bin served long and conducted affairs quietly.
translations.idiomatic: Bin served long and conducted affairs quietly.

sentences.zh: 十三年擢都督僉事，蒞前軍都督府。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was raised to Assistant Commander-in-Chief and took up office in the Front Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was raised to Assistant Commander-in-Chief and entered the Front Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 世襲錦衣僉事。

translations.literal: His line hereditarily held Assistant Commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His line hereditarily held Assistant Commander in the Guard.

sentences.zh: 哈銘從帝還，賜姓名楊銘，歷官錦衣指揮使，數奉使外蕃為通事。

translations.literal: When Ha Ming returned with the Emperor he was granted the surname Yang and the personal name Ming; he rose to Commander of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and several times was sent abroad as interpreter.
translations.idiomatic: When Ha Ming returned with the Emperor he was granted the name Yang Ming; he rose to Guard Commander and often served abroad as interpreter.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，汰傳奉官，銘以塞外侍衛功，獨如故。

translations.literal: When the Xiaozong Emperor succeeded, supernumerary appointees were culled; Ming alone remained as before for his service guarding the Emperor beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong succeeded, supernumerary posts were culled; Ming alone remained for guarding the Emperor beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 以壽卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office at a great age.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at a great age.

sentences.zh: 袁敏者，金齒衛知事也。

translations.literal: Yuan Min was Clerk of the Jinchi Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Min was Clerk of the Jinchi Guard.

sentences.zh: 英宗北征，應募從至大同。

translations.literal: On Emperor Ying's northern campaign he volunteered and followed as far as Datong.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Ying's northern campaign he volunteered and followed to Datong.

sentences.zh: 及駕還，駐萬全左衛。

translations.literal: When the carriage returned it halted at Wanquan Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the carriage returned it halted at Wanquan Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 敏見敵騎逼，請留精兵三四萬人扼其沖，而車駕疾驅入關。

translations.literal: Min saw enemy horsemen pressing close and asked that thirty or forty thousand elite troops be left to hold their thrust while the imperial carriage hurried through the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Min saw enemy horsemen pressing close and asked thirty or forty thousand elite troops hold their thrust while the carriage hurried through the passes.

sentences.zh: 王振不納，六師遂覆。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen would not accept this; the six armies were thereupon destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen would not accept; the six armies were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 敏跳還，上書景帝曰：「上皇曩居九重，所服者袞繡，所食者珍羞，所居者瓊宮瑤室。

translations.literal: Min escaped back and memorialized the Jing Emperor, saying: "The Retired Emperor once dwelt within the Ninefold Enclosure, wearing dragon robes, eating delicacies, dwelling in jade palaces and jeweled chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Min escaped and memorialized the Jing Emperor: "The Retired Emperor once dwelt in the Ninefold Enclosure, wearing dragon robes, eating delicacies, dwelling in jade halls.

sentences.zh: 今駕陷沙漠，服有袞繡乎？

translations.literal: Now the carriage is trapped in the desert—does he wear dragon robes?
translations.idiomatic: Now trapped in the desert—does he wear dragon robes?

sentences.zh: 食有珍羞乎？

translations.literal: Does he eat delicacies?
translations.idiomatic: Does he eat delicacies?

sentences.zh: 居有宮室乎？

translations.literal: Does he dwell in palaces?
translations.idiomatic: Does he dwell in palaces?

sentences.zh: 臣聞之，主辱臣死。

translations.literal: I have heard that when the lord is shamed the minister dies.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard: when the lord is shamed the minister dies.

sentences.zh: 上皇辱至此，臣子何以為心，臣不惜碎首刳心。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor is shamed to this degree—what heart can subjects have? I do not spare smashing my head or cutting out my heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor shamed so—what heart can subjects have? I do not spare my life.

sentences.zh: 乞遣官一人，或就令臣賫書及服御物問安塞外，以盡臣子之義。

translations.literal: I beg that one official be sent, or that I myself be ordered to carry a letter and imperial garments to inquire after his health beyond the passes, to fulfill a subject's duty.
translations.idiomatic: I beg one official be sent, or I be ordered to carry a letter and imperial goods to inquire beyond the passes, fulfilling a subject's duty.

sentences.zh: 臣雖萬死，心實甘之。

translations.literal: Though I die ten thousand deaths, my heart would be glad.
translations.idiomatic: Though I die ten thousand deaths, my heart would be glad.

sentences.zh: 」命禮部議，竟報寢。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites was ordered to deliberate; in the end the report was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites was ordered to deliberate; in the end the memorial was shelved.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：異哉，土木之敗也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Strange indeed was the defeat at Tumu!
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Strange indeed was the defeat at Tumu!

sentences.zh: 寇非深入之師，國非積弱之勢，徒以宦豎竊柄，狎寇弄兵，逆眾心而驅之死地，遂致六師撓敗，乘輿播遷，大臣百官身膏草野。

translations.literal: The raiders were not a deeply penetrating army; the state was not in accumulated weakness—only because eunuchs usurped power, treated raiders lightly and toyed with arms, went against the people's will and drove them to death's ground did the six armies break, the imperial carriage wander in exile, and great ministers and officials of every rank grease the wild grass.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders were not a deep invasion; the state was not weak—only eunuchs usurped power, treated raiders lightly, toyed with arms, defied popular will and drove men to death's ground, so the six armies broke, the carriage wandered, and ministers and officials greased the wild grass.

sentences.zh: 夫始之不能制其不出，出不能使之早旋，枕藉疆場，無益於敗。

translations.literal: At the start they could not restrain the march out; once out they could not make it return early—bodies piled on the frontier, which did nothing to mend the defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At first they could not stop the march; once out they could not bring it home—bodies piled on the frontier, which did not mend defeat.

sentences.zh: 然值倉皇奔潰之時，主辱臣死，誌異偷生，亦可無譏於傷勇矣。

translations.literal: Yet in the hour of frantic rout and collapse, when the lord is shamed the minister dies—those whose intent differed from stealing life need not be reproached for injuring courage.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in frantic rout, when the lord is shamed the minister dies—those who did not steal life need not be reproached for wounding courage.
